title: Release control ticker and incident readiness draft
content:
Date: 2026-03-11
Meeting: Release control weekly sync (standing) — corridor-style notes
Facilitator: Maya Thompson
Attendees: Ethan, Sofia, Daniel, Priya, Arman (SRE), Lina (Product) — partial
Duration: 30m

Agenda (fast):
- Quick health tick (prod metrics)
- Hotfix queue & priority bump requests
- Canary rollouts planned this week + rollback thresholds
- Incident-readiness checklist and runbook gaps
- Action items / owners / blockers

Summary / TL;DR:
- Overall cluster health OK; 95p latency for inference-api bounced to 215ms during a regional spike on 3/10 but returned to baseline after autoscale; observed small increase in cache-miss rate for short-tail prompts.
- Two hotfix candidates (REL-512, INF-4821) approved for expedited pipeline; target deploy windows Friday night and Sunday morning (low traffic).
- Canary policy updated: incremental 5% increments every 10m, automatic rollback if error-rate > 1.5% or 95p latency increases by >40% vs baseline on same region.
- Runbook item: add a rapid-escalation step for model-fallback to smaller quantized variant when GPU mem contention detected.

Production health snapshot (notes):
- inference-api: baseline 95p = 160ms; spike to 215ms during 03/10 14:20-14:50 (region us-west-2).
- runtime-scheduler: CPU throttling observed on small pool hosts after canary job; mitigated by bumping scheduler replicas.
- kv-cache: miss-rate +3.4% for short prompts (<=64 tokens); suspect TTL misconfiguration after previous deploy.

Hotfix queue (prioritized):
1) REL-512 — "scheduler evict race leading to dropped requests"
   - Jira: REL-512
   - Owner: Ethan Park
   - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-scheduler/pull/987
   - Risk: medium (touches eviction logic); rollback: revert to v1.8.2 image
   - Target window: 2026-03-13 02:00-03:00 UTC (low traffic)
2) INF-4821 — "inference-api: cache TTL regression on short prompts"
   - Jira: INF-4821
   - Owner: Sofia Ruiz
   - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1234
   - Risk: low-med (config-only + minor helper change); rollback: config restore
   - Target window: 2026-03-14 08:00-09:00 UTC (pre-weekend)

Canary/rollout rules (applied to both above unless overridden):
- Canary groups: 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%
- Step cadence: 10m between steps; hold on any metric breach
- Abort conditions: 1) error-rate >1.5% in canary cohort 2) 95p latency > baseline*1.4 3) increased tail latency observed in >1 region
- Auto-fallback policy: if rollback triggered, route 100% to canary-compatible smaller model (quantized-x2) until manual rollback cleared.

Incident readiness / runbook gaps discovered:
- Escalation contact list out-of-date: several on-call numbers not included; owner: Daniel Kim to refresh by 2026-03-15 (SRE contact sync).
- Model-fallback sequence is documented but not automated; risk: manual error during nights. Action: Priya to scope automation (runbook -> automation ticket) by 2026-03-18.
- Observability gap: need a dedicated dashboard showing canary cohort vs baseline split by region + model variant. Lina to propose dashboard list; due 2026-03-16.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: cluster-wide OOM if multiple canaries expand concurrently across pools. Mitigation: scheduler will now cap canary host allocation to 20% pool capacity; SRE to enforce via admission control — Arman owns enforcement (SRE-341).
- Risk: cascading retries from clients during deploy windows. Mitigation: add short 503-backoff header to canary responses and coordinate with top 5 customers to inform them of timing. Product will run a customer notification batch; Lina to draft message by 2026-03-12.

Open questions (parking lot):
- Do we want to add a fast-path flag for critical low-latency customers during canary windows? (Trade: complexity vs guaranteed latency) — Next meeting
- Should we increase canary cadence for trivial config-only fixes? Proposal: two-step (50% after 5m) for config-only; need SRE sign-off.

Decisions taken during sync:
- Approve REL-512 hotfix for Friday window; SRE will own preflight and rollback gating.
- Approve INF-4821 for Sunday morning with expedited verification (short smoke suite + perf baseline check).
- Canary thresholds above adopted for this week.

Action items (owner / due):
- Ethan Park: finalize canary job template for REL-512 and run preflight load test (due 2026-03-12) — DONE (preflight passed in staging)
- Sofia Ruiz: prepare deployment runbook snippet for INF-4821 (include TTL revert command) (due 2026-03-13)
- Daniel Kim: refresh escalation contact list + update runbook contacts (due 2026-03-15)
- Priya Nair: scope automation for model-fallback and create ticket with acceptance criteria (Jira: SRE-441) (due 2026-03-18)
- Arman (SRE): enforce canary pool cap and create admission-control rule (Jira: SRE-341) (due 2026-03-13)
- Lina (Product): draft customer notice for Friday night window and coordinate with CX (due 2026-03-12) — IN PROGRESS

Notes & references (scratch):
- Quick link to perf harness: //github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness (internal)
- Postmortem reference: confluence: Release Control - recent regressions index (link in linked_artifacts)
- Short checklist for deploy owners: preflight checklist, smoke suite, canary watch owner, slice owner (latency), rollback command, post-deploy observation 60m

Follow-up: next standing sync same time next week (2026-03-18). If any hotfix moves earlier, update this doc and ping #release-control in slack.

Free-form notes (scratchpad):
- Consider adding a lightweight "deploy severity" tag on PRs so release-engineering can filter urgent changes.
- Might be worth a short runbook drill (15m) next month to practice model-fallback automation path.

End of notes.
